transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (ZenMed Head of ML), Maya Chen (ZenMed Eng Lead), Robert Kim (ZenMed CTO)

Summary:
Quick model catalog demo focused on selecting open models, interpreting benchmark numbers, and understanding Redwood compatibility matrices for ZenMed's POC. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated/VPC tradeoffs, latency vs cost, and next steps for a pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood.
[00:05] Carlos: Hi, Carlos Rivera, Head of ML at ZenMed.
[00:08] Maya: Maya Chen, Engineering Lead.
[00:10] Robert: Robert Kim, CTO.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Sharma, Solutions Engineer, I'll walk through the model catalog and benchmarks.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool, goal for today is walk through model catalog, how you pick open models, what the benchmark numbers mean, and the compatibility matrix — and then see if this maps to your latency/cost constraints for the POC.
[00:30] Carlos: Yeah, we're mainly evaluating lower-cost open models for med record summarization, possibly some hallucination-sensitive flows. Our SLO is sub-300ms p50 for short summaries (<=256 tokens) and cost needs to be < $0.003 per summary ideally.
[00:48] Priya: OK great, that's helpful. I'll start with the catalog UI — we group models by task and verified performance. here is an example page showing model family A (open-quantized) and family B (larger but higher quality). note: some of the auto labels are slightly off in the export, like 'quant' showing as "kwant" sometimes in transcripts — ignore that.
[01:12] [screen share noise] Priya: On the left is the filter for task (generation, summarization, embeddings), you can pick open models only, then we overlay measured latency, token cost, and fidelity scores from our evals. the benchmark rows show p50/p95 latency on rtx-class GPU, CPU fallbacks, and quantized variants.
[01:37] Maya: How do you measure latency? Is that cold-start or warm with kv cache?
[01:42] Priya: Good q. Benchmarks are end-to-end on our standard harness — warm KV cache, continuous batching disabled for p50 numbers, single-request performance. p95 includes some simulated contention. We also provide a separate throughput table with batching numbers.
[01:59] Robert: Are those numbers region-specific? we care about eu-west.
[02:03] Priya: The public catalog is us-west numbers by default, but the matrix includes region multipliers and we can run a quick region-specific benchmark as part of POC.
[02:12] Jordan: Also note the compatibility matrix column — it lists supported runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private), required kernel flags for certain quantizations, and known caveats like kv-cache size or model-specific memory blowups.
[02:23] Carlos: Can you explain the model variants? like quantized FP16 vs int8?
[02:27] Priya: Sure, we surface variants: FP16, dynamic-int8, and some experimental 4-bit modes. For production we recommend dynamic-int8 for many open models to hit cost targets but it depends on sequence length and hallucination risk. the matrix will show quality delta from our eval set.
[02:45] [15s crosstalk]
[02:50] Maya: On privacy - we are PHI. We need VPC deployment, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
[02:57] Jordan: Understood — Redwood Private supports customer VPC with KMS/HSM and audit logs; we have SOC2 attestations and can ship security docs. We'll attach SOC2 and our security pack link.
[03:09] Carlos: Good, and will there be any difference in latency or features for Private?
[03:13] Priya: In general Private has same runtime but network egress and cold-start patterns can differ depending on on-prem or VPC. Also Dedicated reserved capacity gives more predictable p95 latency due to steady GPUs. We'll call out which models are fully supported in Private in the compatibility matrix.
[03:32] Robert: What's the fallback story if a chosen open model underperforms?
[03:36] Jordan: You can route to a smaller/larger variant, or we have automated fallback to a compatible hosted variant. There are also rollout policies for canary and A/B tests.
[03:45] Priya: Also show you the benchmark CSV — columns: model_name, variant, gpu_p50_ms, gpu_p95_ms, tokens_per_second, cpu_fallback_est_ms, quality_score, hosted_supported, dedicated_supported, private_supported, notes.
[04:02] Maya: Can you show an example with a target of 256 tokens?
[04:06] [screen] Priya: Here's model "open-llama-7b-int8" — p50 ~ 180ms on our RTX class GPU at 256 tokens, p95 420ms; cost per 256-token completion ~ $0.0021 on hosted pricing. quality score on our summarization eval is 0.78 relative. note: int8 variant shows slight quality delta vs fp16.
[04:31] Carlos: Those numbers are promising. How reproducible are they on our infra?
[04:35] Priya: We'll run an on-prem or region-specific benchmark during POC using your sample dataset; we recommend including your typical concurrency pattern. we also instrument token-level latency and KV cache hit rates.
[04:48] Robert: What's required to run the region benchmark?
[04:50] Priya: We ask for a masked sample dataset (CSV or NDJSON), expected concurrency, SLOs, and whether you'll use Dedicated or Private. For VPC, we'll need network config and sso info later for security review.
[05:05] Carlos: About hallucination — do you provide evals tied to our prompts?
[05:09] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set evaluations and detect regressions, and the catalog links to those evals. we'll surface regression alerts and compare quality across model variants.
[05:21] Maya: Any notes about tokenization differences across models? we've seen tokenization change output length affecting cost estimates.
[05:27] Priya: Great point — the matrix includes tokenizer family and average tokens per prompt for our eval set. for your prompts we'd run a tokenization pass during POC.
[05:37] Jordan: Let's talk tradeoffs: to meet Carlos's <300ms p50 and cost target, initial suggestion is try an int8 7B open model on Dedicated or hosted with autoscaling. if p95 is too high we can reserve a small Dedicated pool to stabilize latency.
[05:55] Carlos: Budget may push us to hosted first with guardrails.
[05:59] Priya: Hosted is fastest to start. We can do a pilot on hosted, collect perf and quality, then switch to Dedicated for production. the catalog flags models that are recommended for hosted-first pilots.
[06:10] [audio glitch]
[06:15] Maya: For security review, what docs are you going to share?
[06:17] Jordan: SOC2 report, data processing addendum (DPA), SOC2, architecture whitepaper for Redwood Private, and a sample network diagram for VPC peering. We'll share a link to the security pack in the follow-up.
[06:30] Carlos: Can you include pricing for Dedicated commits and an example monthly cost for expected 50k summaries / month?
[06:36] Jordan: Yes — we'll produce a sample pricing sheet. rough back-of-envelope: with int8 7B on hosted at $0.0021 per 256-token summary, 50k/month ~ $105. Dedicated pricing has commit discounts — we'll include two scenarios in the pricing doc.
[06:52] Robert: Are there any gotchas with model licensing for open models?
[06:55] Priya: Most open models have permissive licenses but we flag ones with additional attribution or non-commercial clauses in the catalog notes. we'll surface license text and a quick compatibility note.
[07:08] Maya: Could we get a compatibility matrix that shows kernel flags — like which models need custom kernels or specific cudnn versions?
[07:15] Priya: Yes, the matrix shows runtime requirements (kernel flags, cudnn/driver minimums) and which kernels we use for int8 or 4-bit. For Private on-prem we'll include a hardware checklist.
[07:29] Carlos: Okay excellent.
[07:31] Jordan: Recap — we'll send: compatibility matrix CSV, benchmark sheet with region-adjusted numbers, security docs (SOC2/DPA), and a POC scope draft. Priya will propose perf targets and test harness details.
[07:45] Maya: timeline wise we want to kick POC in April.
[07:49] Jordan: Sounds good. we'll aim to have materials by end of week, and schedule POC scoping for next week.
[07:56] Robert: One more Q: do you support structured outputs or function calling? we want to extract structured JSON from summaries.
[08:02] Priya: Yes — the API supports structured output templates and function/tool calling. we also have structured evals in Optimize to measure schema adherence.
[08:13] Carlos: Great, that helps.
[08:15] Jordan: Any blockers?
[08:17] Maya: We'll need the security attendees list and the masked dataset. otherwise no blockers.
[08:22] Jordan: Perfect. Next steps in notes. Thanks everyone.
[08:27] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hear of model names (open-llama -> open llama, etc.), and token counts approximated in demo.

End of transcript.
